# LinkedIn

Post types for founders: building in public, stories, lessons and more.

30 templates. Square brackets are placeholders: replace every one before you post.

## Building in public

### Feature announcement (`liFeature`)

- Network: LinkedIn
- Use it when: Skip the plain announcement. Show what the new feature makes possible.

```text
We just shipped [feature].

It took us [time], longer than we planned. The reason: [the part that turned out harder than it looked].

What you can do now: [what it makes possible].

What we learned building it: [one lesson].
```

### The plan we changed (`liBuiltWrong`)

- Network: LinkedIn
- Use it when: Share a decision you turned around. It shows you listen before you build.

```text
We were about to build [feature].

Then we talked to [number] customers. [What they told us].

So we built [what you built] instead.

What changed our mind: [the moment or the data].
```

### A request we said no to (`liSaidNo`)

- Network: LinkedIn
- Use it when: Explaining a no makes people trust your yes.

```text
A customer asked us for [feature] this week. We said no.

Not because it is a bad idea, but because [your reason].

What we are doing instead: [your alternative].

Would you have made the same call?
```

### A number we learned from (`liMetric`)

- Network: LinkedIn
- Use it when: A real number says more than a vague claim about growth.

```text
[number] [customers, users or orders] [what happened] last month.

We looked at every single one. The main reason: [reason].

So this month we are [what you are changing].

I will share how it goes.
```

### Our tool stack (`liStack`)

- Network: LinkedIn
- Use it when: People like to see how a company really runs, tool by tool.

```text
Every tool we use to run [company] with a team of [number]:

• [tool]: [what we use it for]
• [tool]: [what we use it for]
• [tool]: [what we use it for]
• [tool]: [what we use it for]

If we could keep only one: [tool].
```

## Your founder story

### Why I started this (`liOrigin`)

- Network: LinkedIn
- Use it when: Tell your origin story every few months. New followers have not heard it yet.

```text
[number] years ago I was [your situation].

I kept asking myself why nobody had built [the thing you missed].

So I started [company].

Today [where you are now]. What has not changed: [the reason you still do it].
```

### A mistake that cost me (`liMistake`)

- Network: LinkedIn
- Use it when: Owning a mistake builds trust faster than a perfect record.

```text
The worst [hiring, product or money] decision I have made: [what you did].

What it cost: [the result].

What I do differently now: [the lesson].
```

### My daily routine (`liRoutine`)

- Network: LinkedIn
- Use it when: Other founders are curious how you keep going.

```text
My daily habits as a founder:

• [habit]
• [habit]
• [habit]

The one I drop on a busy day: [habit].
The one I never drop: [habit].
```

### Advice I ignored (`liIgnoredAdvice`)

- Network: LinkedIn
- Use it when: Everyone has a piece of advice they wish they had taken.

```text
[number] years ago someone told me: [the advice].

I ignored it. Here is what happened:

[what went wrong]

What I would tell myself now: [the lesson].
```

### Unpopular opinion (`liHotTake`)

- Network: LinkedIn
- Use it when: Take a clear stand, then invite the debate. Safe posts get scrolled past.

```text
Unpopular opinion: [your opinion about your field].

Here is why:

[reason one]

[reason two]

Agree or disagree?
```

## Industry commentary

### Take on a trend (`liTrend`)

- Network: LinkedIn
- Use it when: Comment on what your industry is talking about this week.

```text
Everyone is talking about [trend].

What most takes miss: [your point].

What I expect to happen next: [your view].
```

### How it really works (`liExplainer`)

- Network: LinkedIn
- Use it when: Explain something insiders know and outsiders get wrong.

```text
Most people think [common belief].

Here is how it really works:

1. [step or fact]
2. [step or fact]
3. [step or fact]

Once you see it, [what changes].
```

### A prediction (`liPrediction`)

- Network: LinkedIn
- Use it when: A bold forecast gets people talking. Be ready to be wrong.

```text
My prediction: in [number] years, [what will change].

Why I think so:
• [signal one]
• [signal two]
• [signal three]

Save this and check back in [year].
```

### A versus B (`liCompare`)

- Network: LinkedIn
- Use it when: Compare two approaches and say when each one fits.

```text
[approach A] or [approach B] for [use case]?

Pick [approach A] when:
• [situation]
• [situation]

Pick [approach B] when:
• [situation]
• [situation]

We use [your choice], because [reason].
```

### What another company gets right (`liLearnedFrom`)

- Network: LinkedIn
- Use it when: Study a company people respect and pull out a lesson others can use.

```text
[company] does [thing] differently from everyone else in [industry].

What they do: [description].

Why it works: [reason].

What we took from it: [your change].
```

## Team and culture

### Welcome a new hire (`liWelcome`)

- Network: LinkedIn
- Use it when: Celebrate who joins. They share it, and more people see it.

```text
[name] just joined us as [role].

Why I am excited: [a specific reason].

In the first months [first name] will [what they will work on].

Welcome to the team!
```

### A team win (`liTeamWin`)

- Network: LinkedIn
- Use it when: Put the spotlight on your team, not on yourself.

```text
A big thank you to [person or team] for [what they achieved].

The story behind it: [short context].

Why it matters: [the impact].
```

### How we hire (`liHiring`)

- Network: LinkedIn
- Use it when: Explain what you look for when you build a team.

```text
We do not hire for [what most companies look for].

We hire for [what you look for instead].

Why: [the reason, ideally with an example].
```

### A day with us (`liDayInLife`)

- Network: LinkedIn
- Use it when: Show what working with you really looks like.

```text
What our [meeting, ritual or day] looks like:

[short description]

Why we do it this way: [reason].

What we changed after trying it: [lesson].
```

### A value in action (`liValues`)

- Network: LinkedIn
- Use it when: Do not list your values. Show one at work.

```text
One of our values is [value].

Last week it looked like this: [specific example].

It cost us [time, money or comfort], and we would do it again.
```

## Lessons and frameworks

### A framework I use (`liFramework`)

- Network: LinkedIn
- Use it when: Give people a mental model they can use the same day.

```text
How I decide [a common decision]:

1. [question or step]
2. [question or step]
3. [question or step]

If all three point the same way, [what you do].
```

### A book or podcast that changed my mind (`liRecommend`)

- Network: LinkedIn
- Use it when: A recommendation with the reason beats a plain list.

```text
[title] changed how I think about [topic].

The key idea: [one sentence summary].

What I do differently since: [your change].
```

### What I would tell my younger self (`liTellMyself`)

- Network: LinkedIn
- Use it when: A classic format, because it keeps working.

```text
[number] things I would tell myself when I started [company or career]:

1. [lesson]
2. [lesson]
3. [lesson]
4. [lesson]
5. [lesson]
```

### A counterintuitive lesson (`liCounterintuitive`)

- Network: LinkedIn
- Use it when: Question the usual advice, and give the reason.

```text
Something counterintuitive I have learned: [lesson].

Why it is true: [explanation].

When it does not apply: [exception].
```

### A resource to share (`liResource`)

- Network: LinkedIn
- Use it when: Give away something useful, and people come back for more.

```text
Here is the [template, checklist or doc] we use for [purpose].

[the content, or a link]

Take it and make it yours.
```

## Conversation starters

### Ask a question (`liQuestion`)

- Network: LinkedIn
- Use it when: Simple, as long as you ask something people want to answer.

```text
[audience]: what is one [tool, habit or idea] you could not work without?

Mine: [your answer].
```

### Ask for hot takes (`liOpinionPrompt`)

- Network: LinkedIn
- Use it when: Invite others to share their unpopular opinions, and go first.

```text
What is an unpopular opinion you hold about [topic]?

I will go first: [your take].
```

### A poll (`liPoll`)

- Network: LinkedIn
- Use it when: Polls make it easy to take part. Use them now and then, not every week.

```text
What matters more for [audience or stage]?

• [option A]
• [option B]

Vote, then tell me why in the comments.
```

### What would you do? (`liScenario`)

- Network: LinkedIn
- Use it when: Share a real dilemma and let people weigh in.

```text
Scenario: [the situation you faced].

What would you do?

I will share what we did in the comments tomorrow.
```

### Say thank you (`liThanks`)

- Network: LinkedIn
- Use it when: Thank someone who helped. They reply, and their network sees it.

```text
A thank you to [person] for [what they did].

It helped more than they know: [the difference it made].
```
